title: Constraint-Induced Innovation
equation: Constraint Yield = (Resource Limit + Creativity + Time Pressure) ÷ 3
hook: Not having enough money is annoying. It's also why you'll find the clever answer.
statement: Tight resources can force creative breakthroughs that having plenty would never push you toward.
explainer: When you can't throw money or time at a problem, you find the simpler fix. A tiny team or a character limit becomes a design rule, and the product often gets better.
sop: Refuse to solve it by adding more resources.
Brainstorm workarounds, the weirder the better.
Write down what the constraint taught you.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Resource Limit 7, Creativity 6, Time Pressure 8. (7 + 6 + 8) ÷ 3 = 7.0. Higher means the limit is forcing sharper, simpler solutions. Lower means you're just suffering through it without learning anything.
question: Pick one problem and write how you'd solve it with half the budget and half the time.
closing_statement: Limits force the solution abundance lets you avoid.
caption:
Principle Nº 309: Constraint-Induced Innovation

Not having enough money is annoying. It's also why you'll find the clever answer.

Tight resources can force creative breakthroughs that having plenty would never push you toward.

Your turn: Pick one problem and write how you'd solve it with half the budget and half the time.
